title: Property Management Operations Score
subtitle: Find the exact workflows where your team is losing hours every week

persona_selector.text: What best describes your role at the property management company?

answers.label: Owner or founder
Operations lead or COO
Office or property manager
Other team member

questions.text: How are inbound tenant requests (maintenance, general inquiries, complaints) captured today?

answers.label: Phone calls and texts to staff personal numbers, no central log
Shared email inbox, manually triaged each morning
Portal or form, but staff manually re-enter into other systems
Portal feeds directly into our PM software, minimal manual routing
Fully automated intake with AI categorization and auto-routing to the right person

questions.text: How quickly does a typical tenant request get a first response?

answers.label: More than 24 hours, sometimes days
Same business day, but no guarantee
Within 4 to 8 hours during business hours
Within 1 hour during business hours via auto-acknowledgment plus human follow-up
Instant auto-response with status, and human reply within 1 hour

questions.text: When a tenant asks a repeat question (rent due date, lease terms, pet policy), how is it answered?

answers.label: A human types out the answer every single time
Staff copy-paste from a saved doc or email
We have canned responses in our PM software, used inconsistently
Tenant portal FAQ handles most repeat questions, staff handles the rest
AI chatbot or assistant handles 80%+ of repeat questions automatically

questions.text: How do you track communication history with each tenant?

answers.label: Scattered across email, text, phone notes, paper
Mostly in email, occasionally logged in PM software
Logged in PM software when staff remember to
All channels feed into one tenant record automatically
Unified record with AI-generated summaries and sentiment flags

questions.text: How many hours per week does your team spend on tenant communication tasks that feel repetitive?

answers.label: 30+ hours across the team
20 to 30 hours
10 to 20 hours
5 to 10 hours
Under 5 hours

low.headline: Your tenant communication is the single biggest time leak in your business
low.text: You are likely losing 20 to 35 hours a week to manual triage, repeat answers, and chasing replies. The good news is this area gives the fastest ROI when fixed. A simple intake portal plus an AI assistant handling repeat questions can recover 15+ hours a week within 30 days.
steps: Set up a single intake channel (portal or form) and route everything through it for 2 weeks to measure volume
Log the 20 most common tenant questions and draft canned answers for each
Pilot an AI chatbot trained on your lease terms, building rules, and FAQ to handle tier-1 questions automatically

mid.headline: Solid foundation, but you are leaving 8 to 12 hours a week on the table
mid.text: Your team has tools in place, but the workflows are not stitched together. Tenants are getting responses, but staff are still doing too much manual re-entry and triage. The next move is automation between your existing tools.
steps: Audit every place a staff member retypes tenant info from one system to another and list the top 3
Build automations (n8n, Zapier, or native) to eliminate those 3 manual handoffs
Add auto-acknowledgment with expected response time to every inbound channel

high.headline: You are running tenant comms at a level most PM companies do not reach
high.text: Hold this standard and focus optimization elsewhere. The marginal hour saved here is smaller than in other categories. Use the leftover capacity to improve the human touch on high-value tenant moments.
steps: Quarterly review the AI assistant's accuracy and add new FAQ patterns
Identify the 10% of conversations the AI escalates and look for new automation opportunities
Reallocate freed staff time to proactive tenant retention outreach

questions.text: How are new leases created and customized for each unit?

answers.label: From scratch or by copying an old Word doc
From a template, manually edited for each tenant
From a template with merge fields filled in by staff
Auto-generated from tenant and unit data in our system
Auto-generated, auto-sent for e-signature, auto-filed when signed

questions.text: How does lease signing happen?

answers.label: In person or printed and scanned back
PDF emailed back and forth
E-signature tool, but staff manually upload signed copies into PM software
Integrated e-signature that files signed leases automatically
Fully automated: generate, send, sign, file, and trigger move-in workflow

questions.text: How do you track lease renewals and expirations?

answers.label: A spreadsheet someone updates manually
Calendar reminders set by individual staff
PM software shows expirations but no automatic outreach
Automated renewal reminders sent 60 and 90 days out
Automated renewal sequence with offer, follow-up, and signed renewal flowing back to the system

questions.text: When you need to find a specific document (signed lease, addendum, inspection report), how long does it take?

answers.label: 15+ minutes, sometimes we cannot find it
5 to 15 minutes of searching
2 to 5 minutes if filed correctly
Under 2 minutes from the tenant or property record
Instant search across all documents with AI-built query

low.headline: Your lease workflow is costing you rent days and staff sanity
low.text: Slow lease processing means delayed move-ins and lost revenue. Manual document handling also creates compliance risk. A modern lease workflow can cut 5 to 10 days off your average lease-to-occupancy time and free up 6+ hours a week of admin work.
steps: Standardize on one lease template per property type with merge fields for tenant and unit data
Adopt an e-signature tool that integrates with your PM software, not a standalone one
Build an automated renewal sequence starting 90 days before expiration

mid.headline: Lease ops are functional but not yet driving renewal revenue
mid.text: You have signatures and storage handled, but renewals are still a manual push. PM companies that automate renewal sequences typically lift renewal rates 8 to 15% and recover 4 to 6 hours of staff time per week.
steps: Map your current renewal process end-to-end and identify the 3 manual touch points
Build an automated 90-60-30 day renewal sequence with personalized offers
Connect signed leases and renewals to auto-trigger billing, key handoff, and welcome sequences

high.headline: Lease management is fully automated, protect it
high.text: You are operating at the top tier here. Maintain the system and monitor for edge cases that break the automation. Focus your improvement energy on categories with more recoverable time.
steps: Quarterly audit of leases that required manual intervention to find automation gaps
Add AI-built clause review for non-standard leases or addenda
Use freed time to focus on tenant experience improvements at move-in

questions.text: How does a maintenance request get from tenant to vendor?

answers.label: Office manager calls or texts vendors after taking the request
Staff emails vendors and tracks status manually
PM software creates work order, staff assigns vendor manually
Auto-routing rules send most work orders to the right vendor automatically
AI categorizes issue, matches to best vendor, sends work order, and tracks acceptance

questions.text: How do you track work order status and vendor follow-up?

answers.label: Whoever assigned it has to remember to follow up
Weekly meeting where we review open work orders
PM software dashboard, staff checks daily
Automated reminders to vendors and escalations after SLA breach
Real-time tracking with auto-escalation, vendor scorecards, and tenant updates

questions.text: How are vendor invoices received, approved, and paid?

answers.label: Paper or PDF emailed, manually entered into accounting
Email collection, staff matches to work order manually
Vendor portal for invoices, staff approves and exports to accounting
Invoices auto-match to work orders, approval workflow in system
End-to-end: invoice received, AI-matched, auto-approved within rules, paid

questions.text: How do tenants get updates on their maintenance request status?

answers.label: They have to call or email to ask
Staff manually sends updates when they remember
Tenants can check status in the portal
Automated updates sent at each status change
Proactive updates with photos, ETAs, and post-work satisfaction survey

low.headline: Maintenance ops are the second-biggest time drain after tenant comms
low.text: Your team is spending 15 to 25 hours a week on routing, follow-up, and chasing vendors. Tenants are frustrated because they have no visibility. Vendors are slower because there is no accountability system. Automating this area typically returns 12+ hours a week and improves tenant satisfaction scores measurably.
steps: Document your current vendor list with specialties, response times, and pricing
Build auto-routing rules: plumbing goes to vendor A, electrical to vendor B, etc.
Set up automated tenant status updates at: received, assigned, scheduled, complete

mid.headline: Work orders flow, but vendor accountability and tenant visibility need work
mid.text: You have routing in place but the loop is not closed. Vendors are not held to SLAs and tenants still feel in the dark. Closing this loop typically saves 5 to 8 hours a week and reduces tenant complaints by 30 to 50%.
steps: Define SLAs by issue priority (emergency: 2 hours, standard: 48 hours, etc.) and program escalations
Add vendor scorecards based on response time, completion time, and quality
Automate post-completion tenant satisfaction surveys to catch problems early

high.headline: Maintenance ops are dialed in, use it as a competitive advantage
high.text: Your maintenance operation is in the top 10% of PM companies. This is a sales asset when pitching new owners. Document the system so it scales as you grow without degrading.
steps: Build a one-page sales sheet showing your maintenance SLA and tenant satisfaction metrics
Quarterly vendor review using your scorecard data, prune the bottom performers
Pilot predictive maintenance for HVAC, water heaters, and other equipment with known lifecycles

questions.text: How is rent collected and tracked?

answers.label: Checks, cash, and some online payments tracked in a spreadsheet
Most online, but late payments require manual chasing
Online portal with manual late fee assessment
Automated collection with auto-applied late fees and reminders
Fully automated with AI-driven payment plans for at-risk tenants

questions.text: How are owner statements and reports prepared?

answers.label: Manually built in Excel each month
Generated from PM software but heavily edited
Generated from PM software, light formatting
Fully automated generation and delivery on schedule
Automated with AI-written executive summary and benchmarks per property

questions.text: How do you handle accounts payable for property expenses?

answers.label: Paper checks, manual entry
ACH payments, manual entry from invoices
Bills entered in accounting software, paid in batches
Invoices auto-extracted and entered, approval workflow in place
End-to-end automated AP with AI invoice processing and rule-based payments

questions.text: How long does month-end close take?

answers.label: More than 10 business days
5 to 10 business days
3 to 5 business days
1 to 2 business days
Same-day automated close with exception review only

low.headline: Your financial operations are running on manual labor
low.text: Month-end is painful, owner statements eat days, and late rent collection is a part-time job. This is one of the highest-impact areas to automate because the work is rules-based and repetitive. Expect 10 to 15 hours a week recovered and a 5+ day reduction in close time within 60 days.
steps: Move all rent collection to a single online platform with auto-applied late fees
Set up automated payment reminders at day -3, day +1, day +5, and day +10
Implement AI invoice processing (Bill.com, Stampli, or similar) to eliminate manual AP entry

mid.headline: Financial ops work, but they are slower and more expensive than they need to be
mid.text: You have systems but not full automation. The remaining manual work is concentrated at month-end and in exception handling. Targeted automation here typically cuts close time in half and saves 6 to 8 hours a week.
steps: Map every manual step in your month-end close and tackle the top 3 longest ones first
Automate owner statement generation and delivery with personalized commentary
Add AI-built variance analysis to flag unusual P&L items for review before close

high.headline: Your finance function is operating like a much larger company
high.text: You have built infrastructure that most PM companies your size do not have. Use this to take on more doors without adding back-office headcount. The use is real here.
steps: Calculate your back-office cost per unit managed and benchmark it as a sales advantage
Add predictive cash flow modeling for owners based on rent trends and maintenance patterns
Quarterly review of exception items to find new automation rules

questions.text: How are vacant units marketed?

answers.label: We post manually to one or two sites when we remember
Manual posting to multiple sites by staff
Syndication tool pushes listings to major sites
Automated syndication plus AI-written listing copy
Full pipeline: AI copy, professional media, multi-channel ads, retargeting

AI handles qualification, scheduling, and pre-screening end-to-end

questions.text: How are showings scheduled and conducted?

answers.label: Staff coordinates every showing manually by phone
Email back-and-forth to pick a time
Online booking link, in-person showings only
Self-showing tech (smart locks, codes) for qualified prospects
AI-screened, self-guided showings with automated follow-up and application prompt

questions.text: How do you track time-to-lease for vacant units?

answers.label: We do not track it consistently
Tracked manually, reviewed occasionally
Tracked in PM software, reviewed monthly
Dashboard with vacancy days and conversion rates by property
Real-time dashboard with AI-flagged underperforming listings and recommendations

low.headline: Vacancy days are eating your owner relationships
low.text: Every day a unit sits vacant costs your owner real money and erodes their trust in you. Manual marketing and slow inquiry response is costing you 5 to 15 vacancy days per turnover. Modernizing this pipeline typically cuts time-to-lease by 40% and recovers 8 to 10 hours a week of leasing staff time.
steps: Adopt a listing syndication tool that pushes to Zillow, Apartments.com, and 10+ other sites automatically
Set up an AI chatbot or auto-responder to engage prospects within 60 seconds, 24/7
Pilot self-showing technology on 2 to 3 properties to test prospect response

mid.headline: Leasing works, but you are not winning the speed-to-lead game
mid.text: Your competitors with faster response times and self-showings are converting prospects you are losing. Adding 24/7 AI qualification and self-showings typically improves conversion by 25 to 40% and cuts vacancy days by 3 to 7.
steps: Measure your current speed-to-first-response and aim for under 5 minutes
Implement AI qualification that pre-screens budget, move-in date, and basic criteria
Expand self-showing tech to all units where it is legally and physically feasible

high.headline: Leasing pipeline is a competitive moat, lean into it
high.text: You are converting prospects faster than your competition. This is a winning story for new owner pitches and portfolio growth. Document the metrics and use them.
steps: Build a case study showing time-to-lease and conversion rates vs market averages
Add A/B testing on listing copy and photos to keep optimizing
Use the leasing data to advise owners on rent pricing and unit improvements

cta.headline: Get a custom 7-day action plan based on your score
cta.description: Book a 30-minute strategy call and I will walk through your assessment results with you, identify the 2 to 3 automation opportunities that will give you the most hours back, and map out exactly what to build first. No pitch, no obligation, just a real conversation about where your operations are bleeding time and how to fix it.
